content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full source ledger. Below is the result.

**Ledger highlights (traced, no finding raised):**
- Every element of claims 1–16 traces to affirmative disclosure text: branch limit below the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor/connector current sensor/control-pilot interface/local connector identifier; upstream branch current sensor; isolated local bus (claim 5); stored authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy-deficit value; the subtract-reserve/assign-sustaining/distribute-by-deficit allocation; pilot send plus sensor verification; verification-interval shedding in a stored order (claims 1/11) and stopping once below the limit (claims 2/12); triple reclosure conditions (3/13); welded-contactor recording, inhibit of other contactors on the branch and local fault indicator (4/14); network interface, NVM token and last accepted branch limit, outage continuation, non-start of new sessions on an expired/unauthorizing token, tamper-evident meter sequence (6/7/8/15); service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with sensor confirmation before storage (9/10/16).
- Numerals 100–140 and 202–216 each have exactly one meaning, are all used in the description, and every figure-brief numeral name matches the ledger. No numeral is reused for a different part; 106/108/120 recur only for the same parts across FIGS. 1–3.
- Figure geometry is confined to depiction convention (schematic outlines, block placement) except for topology that is source-supported: branch sensor upstream of the contactors (FIG. 1 drops for 120/140 right of 104), bus reaching contactor and control-pilot interface but not the non-charging load, separate solid sensor line and dashed branch-sensor line consistent between FIGS. 1 and 3, contactor in series between branch and vehicle connector with the connector current sensor in that run. No "by way of example" or shape-broadening language appears anywhere in the application text.
- FIG. 4's eight shapes, two-diamond count, branch exits and both return paths match the described flow (210 return to 202, 214 no-fault path to 216, 214 fault path to a terminator, 216 return to 202).

**One defect found:** the FIG. 2 brief ends mid-sentence and drops the leader-placement constraint that FIGS. 1, 3 and 4 all carry.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced: every limitation of claims 1-16, every numeral 100-140 and 202-216 in the ledger and description, every figure brief (FIGS. 1-4) and the Brief Description entries, and the Summary/Detailed Description technical assertions were checked line by line against the affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md. All apparatus structure (contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface, local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor, isolated local bus, network interface, nonvolatile memory, service input, local fault indicator), the allocation sequence (reserve subtraction, minimum sustaining assignment, energy-deficit distribution, pilot send, sensor verification), the staged reduction and ordered contactor shedding on the verification interval, the three reclosure conditions, welded-contactor recording with inhibit and fault indicator, offline token/last-accepted-limit operation, tamper-evident meter sequence, and installer mapping trace to exact disclosure sentences; no dependent-claim limitation or optional embodiment is untraced. Numerals are single-meaning and consistently used; figure topology (sensor upstream of contactors, bus not reaching the non-charging load, dashed branch-sensor line in FIGS. 1 and 3, series contactor-sensor-connector run) matches the description and the source, and no shape-justifying or broadening language appears in the application text. One defect was verified: the FIG. 2 brief terminates in a truncated sentence and omits the leader-placement constraint carried by every other figure brief.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief ends in a truncated sentence and omits the leader-placement constraint
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, last line of the descriptive text immediately before the "## Numerals shown on this figure" heading
findings.detail: The FIG. 2 brief breaks off mid-word and mid-sentence, leaving an incomplete instruction in the deliverable. As a result FIG. 2 alone lacks the statement that the part names are semantic identifiers that do not appear as drawing text, and lacks the leader rule that FIGS. 1, 3 and 4 each carry ("Each reference numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work"). FIG. 2 is the most line-dense view, with seven numerals (108, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130) placed among the incoming supply line, the horizontal run, the sensing line rising from the circle, the joining line to the vehicle connector and both bus branches, so the missing constraint is the one most needed there. This is an unresolved fragment of drafting text, not a technical assertion, and no invention matter is added or removed by completing it.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-2.md reads: "The part names listed below are semantic identifiers onl" (sentence ends there). Compare figures/FIG-1.md: "The part names listed below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each reference numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work." — the same complete pair of sentences appears in figures/FIG-3.md and figures/FIG-4.md.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace the truncated line "The part names listed below are semantic identifiers onl" with the complete text used in the other briefs: "The part names listed below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each reference numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work." Make no other change to the brief.
